'''Bhaya''' is a moribund and possibly extinct [[Indo-Aryan language]] spoken in the lower [[Sindh]] province. According to ''[[Ethnologue]]'',<ref name=e25/> it belongs to the [[Hindi languages|Western Hindi]] subgroup, and possesses considerable lexical and [[Morpheme|morphemic]] similarities with neighbouring languages, but leaves it unclassified beyond this. ''[[Glottolog]]'' classifies it as part of the Western [[Rajasthani languages]] instead.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Bhaya|chapter-url=http://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/bhay1238|editor1-first=Harald|editor1-last=Hammarström|editor2-first=Robert|editor2-last=Forkel|editor3-first=Martin|editor3-last=Haspelmath|year=2025|title=[[Glottolog|Glottolog 5.2]]|edition=|location=Jena, Germany|publisher=Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History}}</ref> An unwritten language, it has often been subject to erroneous, arbitrary, or politically motivated designation as a [[dialect]].
